lead: The clearest production signal is that agent safety increasingly depends on controls around the model: authenticated tool paths, explicit network boundaries and tests that inject failure. Microsoft’s Foundry updates put several of those controls into the managed runtime, with GA and preview status varying by feature; AWS’s resilience pattern tests whether an agent fails safely when its tools return bad data. For your Azure-leaning architecture reviews, separate generally available controls from previews and test the same boundaries in your own identity, network and recovery paths. The ECB also flags AI-related financing and valuation exposure as a financial-stability risk, a reminder that AI governance includes the investment and dependency case, not just model behaviour.

items.title: Resilience testing your agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
items.summary: AWS demonstrates injecting cancelled and corrupted tool results into a deployed Strands agent on Bedrock AgentCore using AWS Fault Injection Service, then observing whether it fails safely or silently. Fault activation is controlled through Systems Manager Parameter Store, and the sample tests the agent while it continues serving traffic; this is a reference implementation, not a reported production benchmark.
items.so_what: Adopt the fault-hypothesis and observability approach in agent release testing, adapting the injected failures and safe-failure criteria to your own critical workflows.

items.title: Hosted agents in Foundry Agent Service at Ignite 2026: from pilot to production inside your enterprise boundaries
items.summary: Microsoft lists shared subnet IPs, network egress controls and recovery for long-running jobs as generally available features in Foundry Agent Service; private CA trust, Azure Policy egress governance and deployment to customer AKS clusters are preview or forthcoming. The post says Azure Policy egress governance starts in three regions, but does not name them in the material reviewed; the AKS preview is targeted for early December 2026.
items.so_what: Adopt the GA egress and recovery controls as a comparison point for your Azure agent-runtime design, and keep preview features out of committed production dependencies until their region and rollout details are confirmed.

items.title: Browser Automation Tool in Microsoft Foundry : Ignite’26 Announcements
items.summary: Microsoft says the Foundry Browser Automation tool, powered by Azure Playwright Workspaces, is generally available with isolated sessions, MCP action batching, Live View and Take control, traces and session recording. Private websites through VNet injection, customer browser proxies, secret management and profile reuse are preview or coming soon; pricing and regions are not stated in the post.
items.so_what: Trial it only for workflows that lack usable APIs, and benchmark its human takeover, session evidence and network isolation against your existing automation controls before relying on preview features.

items.title: Build once, reuse across your agent fleet: Tools and Toolboxes in Foundry
items.summary: Microsoft describes Foundry Toolboxes as a way to curate and version shared tools, skills and agents behind one MCP endpoint, centralise downstream authentication and let agents discover tools on demand. Some announced capabilities are explicitly preview or coming soon, including prompt-agent skill execution and portions of the Work IQ and Fabric IQ integrations; the post does not state pricing or regions.
items.so_what: Trial the shared-tool and central-authentication pattern against your current MCP gateway, with explicit ownership, versioning and credential-rotation tests before broad reuse.

items.title: How Airbnb uses cost per task to operate coding agents on Amazon Bedrock
items.summary: Airbnb describes evaluating coding-agent models on representative engineering tasks, using task quality and list-price token cost per completed task to set model defaults and reasoning-effort ceilings. It pairs those offline evaluations with production CloudWatch measures for latency, throttling, token use and spend; the article says eight new models appeared in about five weeks and that about two thirds of requests used them by mid-October, without presenting a controlled comparison of business outcomes.
items.so_what: Adopt cost per successful task as a model-selection measure, pairing it with production telemetry and a fixed evaluation set rather than choosing from launch benchmarks alone.

items.title: Design responsible AI controls for Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL
items.summary: AWS maps eight Responsible AI dimensions to an Aurora PostgreSQL RAG customer-support design and implements the explainability dimension using citations, source logging, scores and guardrail traces. The post says this is Part 1 and implements one dimension in depth, not a complete treatment of all eight; the example combines Aurora ML, pgvector, Bedrock inference and guardrails.
items.so_what: Use the traceable-answer pattern as a design reference, but treat it as one explainability control and map privacy, authorisation and safety requirements separately in your own architecture.

items.title: Connect Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway to private APIs in a hub-and-spoke network with centralized inspection
items.summary: AWS documents a hub-and-spoke pattern that connects AgentCore Gateway to private APIs and MCP servers while routing traffic through a central firewall and retaining network-team ownership of subnets. The tested lab used three member accounts and one management account in US East (N. Virginia); AWS provides CloudFormation templates, test scripts and validation material in a companion repository.
items.so_what: Trial the ownership and inspection pattern against your network topology, checking every request and response path through the firewall before exposing private tools to agents.

items.title: Private certificate authority support in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity
items.summary: AgentCore Identity now supports private CA certificates when connecting to private identity providers, validating certificates for discovery, JWKS and token endpoints. AWS’s walkthrough stores the public CA certificate in Secrets Manager or S3, uses VPC Lattice for private connectivity, and covers rotation and change protection; the article does not state pricing or supported regions.
items.so_what: Benchmark this against your existing identity-provider integration where private PKI is required, including CA rotation, ownership boundaries and the VPC Lattice dependency.

items.title: v0.24.0
items.summary: OpenAI Agents SDK v0.24.0, dated 15 October 2026 in its release notes, adds run-wide tool-error formatting and MCP discovery annotations and improves recovery, sandbox safety and tracing. It changes compatibility for custom error callbacks and some saved agent graphs; the notes advise finishing affected older graphs on their original SDK rather than treating renaming as migration.
items.so_what: Trial the recovery, tracing and MCP annotation changes against your current agent harness, and test saved-run compatibility before upgrading any long-lived workflows.

items.summary: Promptfoo 0.126.0 adds support for grading with Gemini decision models and restricts saved cloud credentials on POSIX systems, while redacting Azure Storage connection strings in logs and exports. The release changes derived-metric formula handling and says full-repository code scans require Node.js 24 or later, while diff-only scans work on Node.js 22.22 or later.
items.so_what: Benchmark the credential protections and evaluator support against your current evaluation pipeline, and check formula compatibility and Node.js requirements before upgrading.

items.title: Building secure mobile apps in the agentic era
items.summary: Shopify describes changing mobile application security review as AI-assisted coding increased the volume of code it ships, using attack-surface maps, focused AI reviews and checks updated after vulnerabilities are fixed. It reports an average of about 434,000 lines changed per week during a 12-week app rewrite versus about 39,000 per week at the same time the previous year; these are company-reported throughput figures, not an independent security-effectiveness measure.
items.so_what: Trial the feedback-loop and attack-surface review ideas in your secure development lifecycle, but do not use code throughput as evidence that vulnerability risk has fallen.

items.title: Risks from AI valuations, fiscal imbalances and geoeconomic tensions weigh on financial stability outlook
items.summary: The ECB’s November 2026 Financial Stability Review says ambitious earnings expectations for AI firms and debt-funded AI infrastructure investment could expose markets to abrupt repricing and transmit losses between equity and bond markets. It also notes that euro-area banks and non-banks are exposed to AI-related risks; this is a financial-stability assessment, not a new AI compliance rule.
items.so_what: Include provider concentration, financing resilience and dependency risks in AI investment and third-party reviews, without presenting this review as a new supervisory obligation.
